sanskrit: drauṇir uvāca ugraṃ sthāṇuṃ śivaṃ rudraṃ śarvam īśānam īśvaram giriśaṃ varadaṃ devaṃ bhavaṃ bhāvanam avyayam
english: The son of Droṇa said: The fierce one, the immovable, the auspicious Śiva, Rudra, Śarva, Īśāna, the Lord; the dweller of the mountain, the granter of boons, the god, Bhava, the source of being, the imperishable;

sanskrit: śitikaṇṭham ajaṃ śakraṃ krathaṃ kratuharaṃ haram viśvarūpaṃ virūpākṣaṃ bahurūpam umāpatim
english: the dark-throated, the unborn, the mighty, the slayer, the destroyer of sacrifice, Hara; he whose form is the universe, the odd-eyed one, the many-formed, the lord of Umā;

sanskrit: śmaśānavāsinaṃ dṛptaṃ mahāgaṇapatiṃ prabhum khaṭvāṅgadhāriṇaṃ muṇḍaṃ jaṭilaṃ brahmacāriṇam
english: the dweller in the cremation-ground, the exultant, the great lord of hosts, the sovereign; the bearer of the skull-staff, the shaven-headed, the matted-haired, the keeper of holy vows;

sanskrit: manasāpy asucintyena duṣkareṇālpacetasā so 'ham ātmopahāreṇa yakṣye tripuraghātinam
english: him who is hard to conceive even in mind by one of little understanding, hard to attain — I, even I, shall worship the destroyer of the Three Cities with the offering of my own self.

sanskrit: stutaṃ stutyaṃ stūyamānam amoghaṃ carmavāsasam vilohitaṃ nīlakaṇṭham apṛktaṃ durnivāraṇam
english: He who is praised, worthy of praise, being praised; the unfailing, the hide-clad, the blood-red, the blue-throated, the unmingled, the one who cannot be withstood;

sanskrit: śukraṃ viśvasṛjaṃ brahma brahmacāriṇam eva ca vratavantaṃ taponityam anantaṃ tapatāṃ gatim
english: the radiant, the maker of the universe, the Absolute, and the holy celibate; the keeper of vows, ever given to austerity, the endless one, the goal of those who practise penance;

sanskrit: bahurūpaṃ gaṇādhyakṣaṃ tryakṣaṃ pāriṣadapriyam gaṇādhyakṣekṣitamukhaṃ gaurīhṛdayavallabham
english: the many-formed, the overlord of the hosts, the three-eyed, dear to his attendants; he upon whose face the chiefs of the hosts gaze, the beloved of Gaurī's heart;

sanskrit: kumārapitaraṃ piṅgaṃ govṛṣottamavāhanam tanuvāsasam atyugram umābhūṣaṇatatparam
english: the father of Kumāra, the tawny one, who rides the noblest of bulls; the scantily clad, the exceedingly fierce, intent upon the adorning of Umā;

sanskrit: paraṃ parebhyaḥ paramaṃ paraṃ yasmān na vidyate iṣvastrottamabhartāraṃ digantaṃ caiva dakṣiṇam
english: the supreme, higher than the highest, the utmost, beyond whom nothing exists; the master of the finest of bows and weapons, and the very horizon of the south;

sanskrit: hiraṇyakavacaṃ devaṃ candramaulivibhūṣitam prapadye śaraṇaṃ devaṃ parameṇa samādhinā
english: the golden-armoured god, adorned with the moon upon his crown — to that god I go for refuge, with the deepest concentration.

sanskrit: imāṃ cāpy āpadaṃ ghorāṃ tarāmy adya sudustarām sarvabhūtopahāreṇa yakṣye 'haṃ śucinā śucim
english: This dread peril too, so hard to cross, I shall cross this very day; with an offering of all beings, pure myself, I shall worship the Pure One.

sanskrit: iti tasya vyavasitaṃ jñātvā tyāgātmakaṃ manaḥ purastāt kāñcanī vediḥ prādurāsīn mahātmanaḥ
english: Knowing the resolve of that great-souled one, his mind set upon self-surrender, a golden altar appeared before him.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vedyāṃ tadā rājaṃś citrabhānur ajāyata dyāṃ diśo vidiśaḥ khaṃ ca jvālābhir abhipūrayan
english: On that altar, O king, the brilliant-rayed Fire then sprang up, filling heaven, the quarters and the intermediate quarters, and the sky with its flames.

sanskrit: dīptāsyanayanāś cātra naikapādaśirobhujāḥ dvipaśailapratīkāśāḥ prādurāsan mahānanāḥ
english: And there appeared beings with blazing mouths and eyes, with many feet and heads and arms, vast as elephants and mountains, huge of countenance.

sanskrit: śvavarāhoṣṭrarūpāś ca hayagomāyugomukhāḥ ṛkṣamārjāravadanā vyāghradvīpimukhās tathā
english: Some shaped like dogs, boars and camels; some with the faces of horses, jackals and cattle; some with the visages of bears and cats, and some with the muzzles of tigers and leopards;

sanskrit: kākavaktrāḥ plavamukhāḥ śukavaktrās tathaiva ca mahājagaravaktrāś ca haṃsavaktrāḥ sitaprabhāḥ
english: some crow-mouthed, some frog-faced, and likewise parrot-beaked; some with the maws of great pythons, and some swan-faced and gleaming white;

sanskrit: dārvāghāṭamukhāś caiva cāṣavaktrāś ca bhārata kūrmanakramukhāś caiva śiśumāramukhās tathā
english: some with the faces of woodpeckers and blue-jays, O Bhārata; some with the heads of turtles and crocodiles, and some with the snouts of porpoises;

sanskrit: mahāmakaravaktrāś ca timivaktrās tathaiva ca harivaktrāḥ krauñcamukhāḥ kapotebhamukhās tathā
english: some with the jaws of great sea-monsters, and likewise of whales; some lion-faced, some heron-mouthed, and some with the faces of doves and elephants;

sanskrit: pārāvatamukhāś caiva madguvaktrās tathaiva ca pāṇikarṇāḥ sahasrākṣās tathaiva ca śatodarāḥ
english: some pigeon-faced, and likewise some with the bills of cormorants; some whose hands were ears, some thousand-eyed, and some with a hundred bellies;

sanskrit: nirmāṃsāḥ kokavaktrāś ca śyenavaktrāś ca bhārata tathaivāśiraso rājann ṛkṣavaktrāś ca bhīṣaṇāḥ
english: some fleshless, some wolf-faced, and some hawk-visaged, O Bhārata; and some headless, O king, and some with the dread faces of bears;

sanskrit: pradīptanetrajihvāś ca jvālāvaktrās tathaiva ca meṣavaktrās tathaivānye tathā chāgamukhā nṛpa
english: some with eyes and tongues ablaze, and likewise some with flaming mouths; some ram-faced, and others again with the heads of goats, O lord of men;

sanskrit: śaṅkhābhāḥ śaṅkhavaktrāś ca śaṅkhakarṇās tathaiva ca śaṅkhamālāparikarāḥ śaṅkhadhvanisamasvanāḥ
english: some conch-hued, some conch-faced, and likewise some conch-eared; some girt with garlands of conches, their voices like the blast of conches;

sanskrit: jaṭādharāḥ pañcaśikhās tathā muṇḍāḥ kṛśodarāḥ caturdaṃṣṭrāś caturjihvāḥ śaṅkukarṇāḥ kirīṭinaḥ
english: some matted-haired, some with five tufts, and some shaven-headed and lean of belly; some four-tusked, four-tongued, with pointed ears, and some crowned with diadems;

sanskrit: maulīdharāś ca rājendra tathākuñcitamūrdhajāḥ uṣṇīṣiṇo mukuṭinaś cāruvaktrāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: some wearing chaplets, O lord of kings, and some with curling locks; some turbaned, some helmeted, fair of face and richly adorned;

sanskrit: padmotpalāpīḍadharās tathā kumudadhāriṇaḥ māhātmyena ca saṃyuktāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: some wearing wreaths of lotus and water-lily, and some bearing white lilies; and endowed with greatness, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: śataghnīcakrahastāś ca tathā musalapāṇayaḥ bhuśuṇḍīpāśahastāś ca gadāhastāś ca bhārata
english: In their hands they bore the hundred-slaying engine and the discus, and clubs in their fists; some held the bhuśuṇḍi and the noose, and some maces, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭheṣu baddheṣudhayaś citrabāṇā raṇotkaṭāḥ sadhvajāḥ sapatākāś ca saghaṇṭāḥ saparaśvadhāḥ
english: Quivers were bound upon their backs, their arrows of many hues, and they were furious for battle; with banners and pennons, with bells and battle-axes.

sanskrit: mahāpāśodyatakarās tathā laguḍapāṇayaḥ sthūṇāhastāḥ khaḍgahastāḥ sarpocchritakirīṭinaḥ mahāsarpāṅgadadharāś citrābharaṇadhāriṇaḥ
english: With great nooses raised in their hands, and some with cudgels in their grip; some bearing pillars, some swords, their diadems reared up like serpents; wearing armlets of mighty snakes, and decked in ornaments of varied splendour.

sanskrit: rajodhvastāḥ paṅkadigdhāḥ sarve śuklāmbarasrajaḥ nīlāṅgāḥ kamalāṅgāś ca muṇḍavaktrās tathaiva ca
english: Some grimed with dust, some smeared with mire, yet all clad in white garments and garlands; some with dark-blue limbs, some lotus-hued, and some with shaven faces.

sanskrit: bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgāṃs te jharjharānakagomukhān avādayan pāriṣadāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ kanakaprabhāḥ
english: Those attendants, in their joy and golden of hue, sounded kettledrums, conches and tabors, jharjharas, war-drums and cow-horn trumpets.

sanskrit: gāyamānās tathaivānye nṛtyamānās tathāpare laṅghayantaḥ plavantaś ca valgantaś ca mahābalāḥ
english: Some of them sang, and others again danced; the mighty ones leapt and bounded and capered about.

sanskrit: dhāvanto javanāś caṇḍāḥ pavanoddhūtamūrdhajāḥ mattā iva mahānāgā vinadanto muhur muhuḥ
english: Swift and fierce they ran, their hair tossed by the wind, roaring again and again like great elephants in rut.

sanskrit: subhīmā ghorarūpāś ca śūlapaṭṭiśapāṇayaḥ nānāvirāgavasanāś citramālyānulepanāḥ
english: Most terrible they were, and dreadful of form, with pikes and spears in their hands, clad in garments of many colours, with bright garlands and unguents.

sanskrit: ratnacitrāṅgadadharāḥ samudyatakarās tathā hantāro dviṣatāṃ śūrāḥ prasahyāsahyavikramāḥ
english: Wearing armlets bright with jewels, with their arms upraised, those heroes were slayers of foes, irresistible in their unconquerable might.

sanskrit: pātāro 'sṛgvasādyānāṃ māṃsāntrakṛtabhojanāḥ cūḍālāḥ karṇikālāś ca prakṛśāḥ piṭharodarāḥ
english: Drinkers of blood and marrow and such, feeding upon flesh and entrails; some crested, some with great earlocks, some emaciated, some pot-bellied.

sanskrit: atihrasvātidīrghāś ca prabalāś cātibhairavāḥ vikaṭāḥ kālalamboṣṭhā bṛhacchephāsthipiṇḍikāḥ
english: Some very short, some very tall, mighty and exceedingly fearful; misshapen, with dark pendulous lips, with huge members and knots of bone.

sanskrit: mahārhanānāmukuṭā muṇḍāś ca jaṭilāḥ pare sārkendugrahanakṣatrāṃ dyāṃ kuryur ye mahītale
english: Some wore precious crowns of varied kinds, some were shaven, and others matted-haired — such as could fashion upon the earth a heaven with sun, moon, planets and stars,

sanskrit: utsaheraṃś ca ye hantuṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ caturvidham ye ca vītabhayā nityaṃ harasya bhrukuṭībhaṭāḥ
english: and who could dare to destroy the fourfold host of living things; ever free from fear, those warriors of Hara's frown,

sanskrit: kāmakārakarāḥ siddhās trailokyasyeśvareśvarāḥ nityānandapramuditā vāgīśā vītamatsarāḥ
english: doers of their own will, perfected, lords over the lords of the three worlds; ever exultant in eternal bliss, masters of speech, devoid of envy;

sanskrit: prāpyāṣṭaguṇam aiśvaryaṃ ye na yānti ca vismayam yeṣāṃ vismayate nityaṃ bhagavān karmabhir haraḥ
english: who, though they had won the eightfold lordly power, knew no wonder at it; at whose deeds the blessed Hara himself forever marvels;

sanskrit: manovākkarmabhir bhaktair nityam ārādhitaś ca yaiḥ manovākkarmabhir bhaktān pāti putrān ivaurasān
english: by whom, in thought, word and deed, with devotion, he is ever worshipped, and who in thought, word and deed protects his devotees as a father his own sons;

sanskrit: pibanto 'sṛgvasās tv anye kruddhā brahmadviṣāṃ sadā caturviṃśātmakaṃ somaṃ ye pibanti ca nityadā
english: others again, wrathful, ever drinking the blood and marrow of the haters of the sacred, and who forever drink the Soma made of the four-and-twenty principles.

sanskrit: śrutena brahmacaryeṇa tapasā ca damena ca ye samārādhya śūlāṅkaṃ bhavasāyujyam āgatāḥ
english: By sacred learning, by celibacy, by penance and by self-restraint they had propitiated the Trident-marked, and so attained oneness with Bhava.

sanskrit: yair ātmabhūtair bhagavān pārvatyā ca maheśvaraḥ saha bhūtagaṇān bhuṅkte bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ
english: With these, who had become his very self, the blessed Maheśvara, lord of past, future and present, together with Pārvatī, enjoys the hosts of beings.

sanskrit: nānāvicitrahasitakṣveḍitotkruṣṭagarjitaiḥ saṃnādayantas te viśvam aśvatthāmānam abhyayuḥ
english: Filling the whole world with their manifold and wondrous laughter, their hissing, shrieking and roaring, they came toward Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: saṃstuvanto mahādevaṃ bhāḥ kurvāṇāḥ suvarcasaḥ vivardhayiṣavo drauṇer mahimānaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Praising the Great God, radiant and shedding light, eager to magnify the glory of the great-souled son of Droṇa,

sanskrit: jijñāsamānās tattejaḥ sauptikaṃ ca didṛkṣavaḥ bhīmograparighālātaśūlapaṭṭiśapāṇayaḥ ghorarūpāḥ samājagmur bhūtasaṃghāḥ samantataḥ
english: and longing to test his might and to behold the slaughter of the sleeping host — the hordes of beings, fearful of form, bearing dreadful clubs, firebrands, pikes and spears in their hands, gathered there from every side.

sanskrit: janayeyur bhayaṃ ye sma trailokyasyāpi darśanāt tān prekṣamāṇo 'pi vyathāṃ na cakāra mahābalaḥ
english: Though the very sight of them might strike terror into the three worlds, the mighty one, even as he looked upon them, felt no dismay.

sanskrit: atha drauṇir dhanuṣpāṇir baddhagodhāṅgulitravān svayam evātmanātmānam upahāram upāharat
english: Then the son of Droṇa, bow in hand, his fingers guarded by the leathern fence, offered up his own self with his own self as the oblation.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi samidhas tatra pavitrāṇi śitāḥ śarāḥ havir ātmavataś cātmā tasmin bhārata karmaṇi
english: His bow was the kindling-wood, his keen arrows the sacred sprigs, and the self of that self-possessed one was the offering in that rite, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ saumyena mantreṇa droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān upahāraṃ mahāmanyur athātmānam upāharat
english: Then with a gentle hymn the valorous son of Droṇa, in his great wrath, offered up himself as the oblation.

sanskrit: taṃ rudraṃ raudrakarmāṇaṃ raudraiḥ karmabhir acyutam abhiṣṭutya mahātmānam ity uvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Having praised that Rudra, the doer of terrible deeds, unfailing in his terrible works, the great-souled one, with joined palms, spoke thus:

sanskrit: imam ātmānam adyāhaṃ jātam āṅgirase kule agnau juhomi bhagavan pratigṛhṇīṣva māṃ balim
english: "This self of mine, born this day in the line of Aṅgiras, I offer into the fire, O Lord; accept me as thy sacrifice."

sanskrit: bhavadbhaktyā mahādeva parameṇa samādhinā asyām āpadi viśvātmann upākurmi tavāgrataḥ
english: "Out of devotion to thee, O Great God, with the deepest concentration, in this hour of peril, O Soul of all, I make this offering before thee."

sanskrit: tvayi sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvabhūteṣu cāsi vai guṇānāṃ hi pradhānānām ekatvaṃ tvayi tiṣṭhati
english: "In thee abide all beings, and in all beings dwellest thou; in thee rests the unity of the foremost qualities."

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāśaya vibho havirbhūtam upasthitam pratigṛhāṇa māṃ deva yady aśakyāḥ pare mayā
english: "O thou refuge of all beings, all-pervading Lord, here stands the oblation made ready; accept me, O god, if my foes are not to be vanquished by me."

sanskrit: ity uktvā drauṇir āsthāya tāṃ vedīṃ dīptapāvakām saṃtyaktātmā samāruhya kṛṣṇavartmany upāviśat
english: Having spoken thus, the son of Droṇa, mounting that altar of blazing fire and renouncing his very self, took his seat within the path of the Dark-tracked Flame.

sanskrit: tam ūrdhvabāhuṃ niśceṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā havir upasthitam abravīd bhagavān sākṣān mahādevo hasann iva
english: Beholding him, his arms upraised and motionless, set there as the oblation, the blessed Great God himself, as though smiling, spoke:

sanskrit: satyaśaucārjavatyāgais tapasā niyamena ca kṣāntyā bhaktyā ca dhṛtyā ca buddhyā ca vacasā tathā
english: "By truth, purity, uprightness and renunciation, by austerity and self-discipline, by patience, by devotion, by steadfastness, by understanding, and likewise by speech,"

sanskrit: yathāvad aham ārāddhaḥ kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā tasmād iṣṭatamaḥ kṛṣṇād anyo mama na vidyate
english: "I have been duly worshipped by Kṛṣṇa, whose deeds are untiring; therefore none is dearer to me than Kṛṣṇa."

sanskrit: kurvatā tasya saṃmānaṃ tvāṃ ca jijñāsatā mayā pāñcālāḥ sahasā guptā māyāś ca bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ
english: "To do him honour, and to put thee to the test, I have shielded the Pāñcālas all this while, and wrought many an illusion."

sanskrit: kṛtas tasyaiṣa saṃmānaḥ pāñcālān rakṣatā mayā abhibhūtās tu kālena naiṣām adyāsti jīvitam
english: "This honour I have shown him by guarding the Pāñcālas; but now they are overtaken by Time, and their span of life is at an end this day."

sanskrit: evam uktvā maheṣvāsaṃ bhagavān ātmanas tanum āviveśa dadau cāsmai vimalaṃ khaḍgam uttamam
english: Having spoken thus to the great archer, the Lord entered into his body, and gave to him a stainless and excellent sword.

sanskrit: athāviṣṭo bhagavatā bhūyo jajvāla tejasā varṣmavāṃś cābhavad yuddhe devasṛṣṭena tejasā
english: Then, possessed by the Lord, he blazed anew with splendour, and in the fight he grew vast in stature through the god-given energy.

sanskrit: tam adṛśyāni bhūtāni rakṣāṃsi ca samādravan abhitaḥ śatruśibiraṃ yāntaṃ sākṣād iveśvaram
english: Unseen beings and demons thronged about him on every side as he went toward the enemy's camp, like the Lord himself made manifest.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā prayāte śibiraṃ droṇaputre mahārathe kaccit kṛpaś ca bhojaś ca bhayārtau na nyavartatām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the great warrior, the son of Droṇa, had thus set out for the camp, did not Kṛpa and the Bhoja chieftain turn back, stricken with fear?

sanskrit: kaccin na vāritau kṣudrai rakṣibhir nopalakṣitau asahyam iti vā matvā na nivṛttau mahārathau
english: Were the two great warriors not held back, unmarked by the lowly sentinels? Or, deeming the task unbearable, did they not turn away?

sanskrit: kaccit pramathya śibiraṃ hatvā somakapāṇḍavān duryodhanasya padavīṃ gatau paramikāṃ raṇe
english: Or did they, having crushed the camp and slain the Somakas and Pāṇḍavas, follow Duryodhana upon his highest road in battle?

sanskrit: pāñcālair vā vinihatau kaccin nāsvapatāṃ kṣitau kaccit tābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ karma tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Or, slain by the Pāñcālas, do they not now lie asleep upon the earth? Whatever the deed those two have done, tell it to me, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin prayāte śibiraṃ droṇaputre mahātmani kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca śibiradvāry atiṣṭhatām
english: Saṃjaya said: When the great-souled son of Droṇa had set out for the camp, Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman took their stand at the gate of the camp.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu tau dṛṣṭvā yatnavantau mahārathau prahṛṣṭaḥ śanakai rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Aśvatthāman, seeing those two great warriors ready and resolute, rejoiced, O king, and softly spoke these words:

sanskrit: yattau bhavantau paryāptau sarvakṣatrasya nāśane kiṃ punar yodhaśeṣasya prasuptasya viśeṣataḥ
english: "You two, exerting yourselves, would suffice to destroy the whole warrior race; how much more, then, this remnant of fighters, and they fast asleep?"

sanskrit: ahaṃ pravekṣye śibiraṃ cariṣyāmi ca kālavat yathā na kaś cid api me jīvan mucyeta mānavaḥ
english: "I will enter the camp and range through it like Death itself, that no living man may escape from me."

sanskrit: ity uktvā prāviśad drauṇiḥ pārthānāṃ śibiraṃ mahat advāreṇābhyavaskandya vihāya bhayam ātmanaḥ
english: Having said this, the son of Droṇa, casting off all fear, leapt over the wall and entered the great camp of the Pārthas, not by the gate.

sanskrit: sa praviśya mahābāhur uddeśajñaś ca tasya ha dhṛṣṭadyumnasya nilayaṃ śanakair abhyupāgamat
english: The mighty-armed one, having entered and knowing the place well, softly approached the dwelling of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: te tu kṛtvā mahat karma śrāntāś ca balavad raṇe prasuptā vai suviśvastāḥ svasainyaparivāritāḥ
english: But those men, having wrought great feats and grown sorely weary in the battle, lay deep in slumber, wholly at their ease, encircled by their own troops.

sanskrit: atha praviśya tad veśma dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhārata pāñcālyaṃ śayane drauṇir apaśyat suptam antikāt
english: Then, entering the chamber of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O Bhārata, the son of Droṇa beheld the prince of Pāñcāla asleep upon his couch close at hand,

sanskrit: kṣaumāvadāte mahati spardhyāstaraṇasaṃvṛte mālyapravarasaṃyukte dhūpaiś cūrṇaiś ca vāsite
english: upon a great bed bright with fine linen, spread with coverlets fit for envy, adorned with choice garlands, and made fragrant with incense and aromatic powders.

sanskrit: taṃ śayānaṃ mahātmānaṃ visrabdham akutobhayam prābodhayata pādena śayanasthaṃ mahīpate
english: That great-souled one, lying there at ease and fearing nothing, asleep upon his bed, he awakened with his foot, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: sa buddhvā caraṇasparśam utthāya raṇadurmadaḥ abhyajānad ameyātmā droṇaputraṃ mahāratham
english: Roused by the touch of the foot, that one, fierce in battle and of immeasurable spirit, rose up and knew him for the son of Droṇa, the great warrior.
